=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_autofix_step_push_pending_commits.sh:16 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The script uses `if [[ "${TARGET_BRANCH:-}" =~ ^auto/update-workflows-[0-9a-f]{12}(-r[2-5])?$ ]]; then`, which depends on `TARGET_BRANCH` being set.
  WHY: The reviewer says that if `TARGET_BRANCH` is unset, `bash -u` raises an `unbound variable` error and exits, so the autofix cannot push commits; the reviewer also notes that the `${TARGET_BRANCH:-}` default is already present and suggests `[[ -n "${TARGET_BRANCH:-}" ]]` as safer (source severity MAJOR).
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_merge_validate_dispatch.sh:147 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `gh workflow run ... || { [ "${validate_workflow}" != "internal-validate.yml" ] && gh workflow run "internal-validate.yml" ... }` fallback does not check that `validate_workflow` exists before the first dispatch.
  WHY: The reviewer calls the fallback logic itself sound (if both dispatches fail, `validation_dispatch_failed=1` is set), but an invalid `validate_workflow` filename makes the first dispatch fail every time before the fallback runs (source severity NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A workflow that comes within 30,000 bytes of the 430,000-byte test ceiling opens an `ai:ci-budget` issue before any test fails." (issue #10166, "Goal" section)
  expected_change_site: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `budget-watch` job — its trigger and ordering/execution order relative to the test jobs
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `budget-watch` is still restricted to `on: push: branches: [main]` (line 19) and runs only after the test jobs complete (line 5136), with the job's `if:` predicate requiring `github.event_name == 'push'` and `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, and it depends on the test jobs (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:5095-5111`); it never runs for pull-request runs, so a PR that takes a workflow from below 400,000 bytes to above 430,000 bytes gets no `ai:ci-budget` issue before its contract test fails; per minimax, the fix should extend the existing job's trigger (e.g. a `pull_request` event filter plus an ordering change) rather than add a new job, because §33 forbids new jobs; five prior editor rounds deferred this gap, and the issue's goal text is unchanged; all three reviewers rated it severity MAJOR. Note: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash reviewed this gap and declined to raise it (see their sections).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
(No findings reported.)
- NOTE (task gap rejected): Skipped pass 1's gap that the budget-watch job runs only on push to main and has no PR trigger. Issue #10166's "Automation and wiring" section names "the existing `budget-watch` job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`" and says "Runner use (§33): no new job, workflow or matrix leg". The diff implements that design: the ci.yml fallback is '400000', DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_WARN_BYTES is 400_000 and WORKFLOW_TEST_CEILING_BYTES is 430_000. Adding a PR trigger would go beyond the issue.
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: tests/test_review_autofix_step_fallback_verify.py | the module-level SUPPORT_CHECKOUT_WRAPPER_STEPS / the parametrize on test_support_checkout_job_wrapper_sources_only_the_verified_checkout | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
  PROBLEM: If the registry is empty, pytest collects zero cases and the in-test `assert SUPPORT_CHECKOUT_WRAPPER_STEPS` never runs.
  WHY: test_review_autofix_step_scripts_contract.py::test_support_checkout_job_step_scripts_come_only_from_their_verified_checkout already asserts the registry is non-empty, so this matters only if that test is removed. Suggested fix: add `def test_support_checkout_wrapper_steps_registered(): assert len(SUPPORT_CHECKOUT_WRAPPER_STEPS) == 2` (2 lines).

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- HARDENING_SUGGESTION: tests/test_review_autofix_step_fallback_verify.py — line just after `@pytest.mark.parametrize(...)` (the in-function `assert SUPPORT_CHECKOUT_WRAPPER_STEPS, "..."`) | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
  PROBLEM: `assert SUPPORT_CHECKOUT_WRAPPER_STEPS, "support-checkout step registry must not be empty"` inside `test_support_checkout_job_wrapper_sources_only_the_verified_checkout` is unreachable when the registry is empty, because parametrize then collects zero cases and the test passes silently.
  WHY: The assert looks like a runtime safeguard but provides none; the empty case is already caught by `tests/test_review_autofix_step_scripts_contract.py::test_support_checkout_job_step_scripts_come_only_from_their_verified_checkout`. Suggested fix: (a) move the assert to module scope next to `SUPPORT_CHECKOUT_WRAPPER_STEPS = sorted(...)`, or (b) delete it as redundant (1-2 lines).
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: "A workflow that comes within 30,000 bytes of the 430,000-byte test ceiling opens an `ai:ci-budget` issue before any test fails." (issue #10166, "Goal" section).
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `budget-watch` job — its trigger and ordering relative to the test jobs.
  Evidence of absence: `budget-watch` runs only when `github.event_name == 'push'` and `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` (the job's `if:` predicate), and after the size tests, so it never runs for PRs. A PR that takes a workflow from below 400,000 bytes to above 430,000 bytes gets no `ai:ci-budget` issue before the contract test fails. The fix should extend the existing job (e.g. a `pull_request` event filter plus an ordering change), not add a new job, per §33. Five prior editor rounds deferred this; the issue's goal text is unchanged, so the gap remains.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  PROBLEM: Unlike every codex-agent wrapper's #10208 verify line (`env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE git -C ...`), these two wrappers read the checkout HEAD without clearing `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`.
  WHY: Neither job currently exports those variables, and a failure exits 1 (fails closed), so this is a consistency issue only; the test does not cover the GIT_DIR case. Suggested fix: prefix both rev-parse checks with `env -u GIT_DIR -u GIT_WORK_TREE` (2 lines).
